name: Lombard (Dwarf Legendary Inquisitor Archetype)
body:
Lombards (Long-beards) are religious bankers who guide civilizations through the manipulation of wealth. As borrowers and lenders, they broker deals with friends and enemies alike in order to pave the way to progress. Woe to those who fail to settle their debts with a lombard, for such debtors are under the lombard’s power.

Requirements

Alignment: A lombard must be of a lawful alignment.

Class Features

Invest Treasure: Once per level, a lombard can give a portion of her treasure to her church’s bank to store for safekeeping. The church adds a 2% interest to the portion for legendary inquisitor each level the lombard gains, until the lombard chooses to withdraw the portion.

For example: If a 4th level lombard gives a 5,000 gp portion of treasure to her church, then later achieves 12th level, her 5,000 gp portion is increased by 16%, making it 6,600 gp.

A lombard can have multiple portions stored for safekeeping at a time.

This replaces domain.

Usurer (Su)

At 4th level, a lombard can willingly loan her money to creatures that are capable of understanding the concept of lending and owing (minimum Intelligence 8).

Creatures that owe a lombard money take a penalty to their Armor Class against the lombard’s attacks and to saving throws against the lombard’s spells and class abilities. These penalties are equal to -1 per every 1,000 gp owed (maximum -5).

This replaces the daily use of judgment gained at 4th level.

Exploit Desperation (Ex)

At 14th level, as a swift action that does not provoke attacks of opportunity, a lombard can toss a handful of gold coins at an opponent as a ranged attack, with a maximum range of 10 feet. If the attack hits, and the opponent is a creature that collects treasure, the opponent becomes affected according to the number of gold coins tossed.

Table 3-2: Gold Coins and Effects
Amount of Gold Coins	Effect
3	-10 foot penalty for 1 round.
10	-1 to AC and 15 foot penalty for 2 rounds.
250	1d6 bludgeoning damage, -2 to AC and 15 foot penalty for 3 rounds.
2,500 or more	2d6 bludgeoning damage, -3 to AC and 20 foot penalty for 3 rounds.

A lombard who attempts to recover coins she tosses with this ability inevitably loses some depending on the environment she is in (GM’s discretion).

This replaces exploit weakness.

Simony (Sp)

At 15th level, a lombard adds atonement to her list of spells known. In addition, the casting time of this spell is reduced to 10 minutes if the target pays for the entire cost of casting this spell.

This replaces the teamwork feat gained at 15th level.
